findings.reason: §2 must be rewritten against the fragment model (or closed as superseded) before any node is cut, or an implementing node will rebuild the shared-path grant the fragment default exists to remove.
findings.text: §2 ("crew dispatch adds three paths to every node ... the node's own plan file, its cumulative evidence record, and a figures directory") describes a grant that shipped as `86aafc6a` and was then replaced: `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1964` now computes those three as the *detection* set only, and its docstring states "They are no longer granted by default, because a grant every node holds is exactly the merge conflict the per-node fragment default removes"; the default is instead the node-keyed fragment at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2015` (`docs/evidence/fragments/<plan>/<node-id>.html`, `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/`), landed by `f6e41cc7d` on 2026-09-28 — after the plan's 2026-09-24 revision. The plan's §2 premise is therefore not merely unbuilt but the design the code moved away from

findings.reason: §4 is largely shipped; the plan should record the existing allowance rule and reduce §4 to the gap that actually remains, if any.
findings.text: §4 ("the contract text ... names the figure as a deliverable") already exists in `reckon/crew/prompts.py:127` (`_artifact_allowance` withholds a figure unless the done-when names one) and the figure convention `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/` is already in `reckon/crew/prompts.py:166`; the plan cites neither

findings.reason: the plan should name one derivation (dispatch's scope machinery) that the gate and the views consume, so the three surfaces cannot drift; §6 already asks for the two `crew complete` gates to be one pass, and the same consolidation applies one layer down.
findings.text: the node's landing paths are a single fact (plan file, evidence fragment, figure fragment for that node id) that §2, §3 and §5 each need, yet the plan gives them no single home: §2 re-derives them in dispatch, §3 re-derives them in the promotion gate, §5 re-derives artifact locations in the views

findings.reason: §5 should state that it extends `run_dir()` and the recovery unmerged-commit walk rather than adding a parallel locator, or the two will disagree on what "unmerged" and "run directory" mean.
findings.text: §5 ("Gate logs move under the run directory") and its "follower and drain views list figures committed in unmerged worktrees" propose a new listing over machinery whose owners exist: `run_dir(run_id)` at `reckon/crew/runs.py:69` already owns run-directory paths, and `reckon/crew/recovery.py:3908` (`_commits_missing_from` / `unmerged_commits`) already enumerates a worktree's unmerged commits

findings.reason: a forked landing-path derivation drifts from the owner that computes claims and peer conflicts, and the fragment default is the shipped answer; the honest change is to extend `_shared_landing_paths`/`_landing_fragment_paths`, not to add a grant beside them.
findings.text: §2's default grant of the plan file, cumulative evidence record and figures topic duplicates the landing-path owner `_shared_landing_paths` (and the fragment default beside it, `_landing_fragment_paths` at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2015`); the plan forks a second notion of a node's landing paths instead of extending the one the exclusive-claim, peer-disclosure and conflict machinery already reads

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the three record mechanisms (§2 grant/refusal, §3 promotion gate, §5 view listing) each re-derive the node's landing paths with no single owner, spreading one behaviour across four surfaces.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 re-implements the landing-path grant that `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` already owns as `_shared_landing_paths` / `_landing_fragment_paths`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes granting three shared landing paths to every node, a mechanism that was built and then deliberately replaced by the per-node fragment default the plan never cites.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5 layers a gate-log relocation and a stranded-artifact listing over `run_dir()` and the recovery unmerged-commit machinery without saying why those owners cannot be extended.
